comment: This is a points-accumulation based class where you can rack up points to get the grade you want. Similar to Prof Spindle, but dates for individual + group assignments overlap a lot. I recommend doing quizzes in advance or during the week that the material is assigned. The earlier you can get stuff knocked out, the better position you'll be in.

Professor Krumwiede is a great guy. The comments here are completely off. He tries so hard every class. The key for this course is to read the book, and come prepared to class. If you do that, the lectures are easy, and the tests are not that bad. He gives weekly online assignments, which are helpful, easy, and really bump your grade if you do them

He may be a nice and caring guy. But this is one of the worst professors I've ever had. His lectures are useless. Makes tons of mistakes. I have done every single exercises in the textbook and I got C! Really tricky test questions and long at the same time :( AVOID!
He's so nice. He tries to make students do better and open to questions.

He may be a nice and caring guy. But this is one of the worst professors I've ever had. His lectures are useless. He assigns random homework. His weekly tests are impossible they test whether you're a math formula wiz not accounting. He does not prepare for class. Makes tons of mistakes. His tests are impossibly long and trick qh questions.. avoid.
This guy single handedly has the ability to ruin a semester. Avoid at all costs

He is a terrible teacher! He gives hours of homework on chapters that he hasn't gone over and spends a max of 10 mins going over problems the next class. He rushes through the material and always started a new chapter during hte last 5 mins of class. His tests are hard and take longer than the 50 min class period. Also not an understanding person.
The dude tries his best and truly cares about his students.  With that being said, this class is rough and kip's lesson plans are ineffective at best.
Sweet and cares about all students. Very fair, but this class is hard after all.
